intro.patientBody: This is where you check in on your treatment goals — usually once a week. Each check-in takes a couple of minutes, and your clinic sees your answers so they can adjust your care. When something is due you'll see it right here, along with your goals and any notes your care team leaves you.
intro.physiotherapistBody: Unlock a patient with the visit code they show you. You can then record how their treatment goals are progressing, suggest new goals, and flag muscles for the physician to consider at the next injection visit.
intro.clinicianBody: Unlock a patient with their visit code to review goals, record a treatment, and see how the patient and their therapist have rated progress. Patient and therapist suggestions appear on the patient's page for you to act on.
intro.clinicianHowBody: You unlock one patient at a time with the visit code they bring. The session stays open while you work and times out when you are done, so the next patient starts clean. This app is a shared space for goals and progress — it is not your clinical record, and it does not diagnose, dose, or replace your usual notes.
intro.physiotherapistHowBody: You unlock one patient at a time with their visit code. While the session is open you record progress on their goals, suggest new goals or muscles for the physician to consider, and can record assistive devices in the patient's information. Your own clinical notes stay in your usual record system.
intro.comfortBody: Set the text size and light or dark mode so the app is easy on your eyes. You can change these anytime from the menu in the top corner.
intro.comfortWhereHint: You can change these anytime from the menu in the top corner.
intro.graphBody: Each goal has its own graph, week by week. An NRS goal plots the raw 0–10 score the patient reported. A GAS goal uses five descriptive bands — an outcome level, not a score. Both show the patient’s line and the therapist’s.
intro.graphSampleGoalNrs: Walk a little further each week
intro.graphTryHint: Tap any dot to see that week's rating and any note. The sage line is the patient's own rating; the amber line is the therapist's assessment. A grey ring marks a week that was skipped.
intro.graphSampleGoal: Hold a cup of tea steadily
intro.actionsBodyClinician: From a patient's page these open inline: patient suggestions to review, therapist input, the cross-cycle history, and the EHR export.
intro.actionsBodyTherapist: From a patient's page you can report progress, suggest goals or muscles for the physician, and record assistive devices in the patient's information.
intro.recordBodyClinician: Record what you injected — date, product, dilution, guidance, and the muscles with their doses. The total is entered after the muscle list. If there was a previous treatment, you can copy it into the form with one tap and adjust from there. This becomes the patient's treatment record for the cycle.
intro.recordBodyTherapist: Rate how each goal is progressing and add a short note for the physician to see at the next visit. The patient's own ratings stay separate from yours.
intro.checkinBody: Once a week you rate how each goal went — some goals use a 0–10 scale, others a few options from “much worse” to “much better.” You’ll also mark which days you did your exercises, at home and with a therapist, and once during your cycle we may ask for a short, optional video — you’ll always be asked first. It takes a couple of minutes, and your care team sees your answers so they can adjust your treatment.
intro.detailsBody: This helps your care team and, in anonymous form, supports research. Both are optional — you can skip and add them later in your profile.
intro.visitBody: When you see your clinician or therapist, open “Show visit code” and show or read them the code. That lets them open your record for the visit.

help.patientHomeBody: This is your home screen. When a weekly check-in is due it appears at the top — tap it to rate how your goals are going (it takes a minute, and your care team sees your answers so they can adjust your treatment). Below it you can open Your goals to see how each one is tracking, and Show visit code when you're at an appointment. If your physician or therapist leaves you a note, it appears here too.
help.goalsBody: Each goal has its own card with a graph of how it's tracking week by week: your own check-in ratings, plus your therapist's assessments where they've added them. Tap a point to see that week's rating and any note. You can also suggest a new goal here — your physician reviews it and sets it up so it joins your weekly check-ins.
help.checkinBody: Rate how each goal went this week — some goals use a 0–10 scale, others a few options from “much worse” to “much better.” You’ll also mark which days you trained, at home and with a therapist, and once in your cycle you may be offered a short, optional video (you’re always asked first). Add a few words if you like — there are no right or wrong answers.
help.clinicianPatientBody: This is your home base for an unlocked patient. Each goal has a graph — NRS goals show the raw 0–10 score, GAS goals use descriptive bands. A collapsible “Training” panel shows which days the patient trained, at home vs with a therapist. Keep a free-text “Since last visit” note here too — it’s tied to the current cycle. The buttons open patient suggestions, therapist input, the cross-cycle history, and the EHR export. Record a treatment from here, and end the session when you step away.
help.treatmentBody: Enter the session details — date, product, dilution, guidance — then add each muscle with its dose. The total goes in below the muscle list, once you've added them all. If the patient had a previous treatment, use Copy last treatment into the form on the Last treatment card to fill everything from last time, then adjust — it's usually the fastest start. Save when done; this becomes the cycle's treatment record.
help.historyBody: These charts show trends across all of this patient’s treatment cycles — total dose, goal outcomes, benefit duration, and re-treatment timing. For GAS goals the coloured bands are descriptive (how a result compares to expected), not a pass or fail; NRS goals show the 0–10 score. It needs at least two cycles to show a trend.
help.newGoalBody: Use this for a goal the patient told you in clinic. Write it in their own words, add your clinical phrasing, then choose how it’s measured: a 0–10 question (NRS) with how the answers map to outcome levels, or five descriptive levels (GAS) from “much worse” to “much better.” You can also turn on an optional short patient video, offered once around weeks 6–8. The goal still belongs to the patient — you’re recording it for them.
help.suggestionBody: A patient has suggested a goal. Read it in their words, then approve it as-is, edit and approve, or set it aside to discuss. Approving opens the rating setup — choose a 0–10 question (NRS) or five descriptive levels (GAS) — so the goal becomes part of their weekly check-ins.
help.physioPatientBody: This is your home base for an unlocked patient. The graphs show how each goal is progressing — your assessments and the patient's own ratings. From here you can report progress, suggest goals or muscles for the physician, and record assistive devices in the patient's information.
help.physioProgressBody: Rate how each goal is progressing and add a short note for the physician to see at the next visit. Your assessment is kept separate from the patient's own weekly ratings, so both points of view stay visible on the graph.

notifications.title: Get reminded about your weekly check-in
notifications.body: We’ll send a notification to this device when your check-in is due, and one reminder if it’s a couple of days late. Nothing else.
notifications.denied: Notifications were blocked. To turn them on later, open your browser settings for this site and allow notifications.
notifications.iosStep1: Tap the Share button at the bottom of Safari (the square with the arrow).
notifications.iosStep2: Scroll down and tap “Add to Home Screen”.
notifications.iosStep3: Open the app from the home screen, sign in, and tap “Enable notifications” again.
notifications.notConfigured: Notifications are not configured (missing VAPID key).
notifications.dayBody: Pick a day to be reminded about your check-in. We'll send one gentle notification that day.
notifications.dayChangeNote: You can change this anytime in settings.

login.title: Sign in

login.errNotActivated: This account isn’t activated yet. Please contact your clinic.

login.errNetwork: Network problem. Check your connection and try again.

forgotPassword.title: Reset your password
forgotPassword.intro: Enter the email your clinic has for you. We’ll send a link to reset your password.
forgotPassword.sentBody: If an account exists for that email, we’ve sent a link to reset your password. If it doesn’t arrive, check your spam folder or contact your clinic.
forgotPassword.errRateLimit: Too many requests. Please wait a minute and try again.
forgotPassword.errGeneric: Could not send the reset email. Please try again.

resetPassword.introForced: Your account was set up with a temporary password. Choose your own so it’s easy for you to remember.
resetPassword.introNormal: Choose a new password for your account.
resetPassword.errTooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
resetPassword.errSameAsCurrent: Please choose a password different from your current one.
resetPassword.errGeneric: Could not update your password. Please try again.

videoConsent.withdrawNote: You can change or withdraw your consent at any time in your profile.

researchConsent.helper: Whether this patient's data may be used for research. The study export only includes patients who have consented.

researchConsent.withdrawNote: Withdrawing stops the study export immediately. Records already shared are removed once an administrator confirms deletion.
researchConsent.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw this patient's research consent? The study export will stop immediately, and shared records are removed once an administrator confirms deletion.
